abstract: Maintains dive survey monitoring protocols and seabed turbidity impact assessments
system_message:
You are the Benthic Ecology and Permitting Lead (BEP). Your business responsibilities include maintaining dive survey monitoring protocols and seabed turbidity impact assessments, as well as overseeing acoustic water column profiling technical specifications for restoration candidate contractors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Acoustic water column profiling（HYDRO）
information_points.content:
BEP-HYDRO-PLI：Cascadia Benthic Solutions operates a mounted bottom-tracking acoustic sensor array with an acoustic Doppler profiler beam frequency of 600 kHz for shallow current mapping.
BEP-HYDRO-DL3：Pacific Kelp Restoration Group operates a mounted bottom-tracking acoustic sensor array configured with an acoustic Doppler profiler beam frequency of 1200 kHz for shallow current mapping.
BEP-HYDRO-O47：Salish Sound Marine Works utilizes a mounted bottom-tracking acoustic sensor array with an acoustic Doppler profiler beam frequency of 300 kHz for shallow current mapping.

information_points.title: Maintains dive survey monitoring protocols and seabed turbidity impact assessments（ECOL）
information_points.content:
BEP-ECOL-38F：For Cascadia Benthic Solutions, the scientific dive survey protocol is approved under state regulatory review, and the modeled maximum benthic turbidity plume reaches a peak of 18 NTU five meters from substrate anchor and tile-placement arrays.
BEP-ECOL-ED4：For Salish Sound Marine Works, the scientific dive survey protocol is approved according to the Washington State resource agency compliance review, and the maximum benthic turbidity plume reaches a peak of 10 NTU at five meters from substrate anchor and tile-placement arrays.
BEP-ECOL-OE6：For Pacific Kelp Restoration Group, the scientific dive survey protocol is approved by resource agency compliance, and the modeled maximum benthic turbidity plume reaches a peak of 14 NTU at five meters from substrate anchor and tile-placement arrays.
